chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Humran, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'In what do the people differ?' I said, 'They claim that cupping on Tuesday is more beneficial.' He said to me: 'And to what do they attribute this?' I said, 'They claim it is the day of blood.' He said: 'They are right. So it is more likely that one should not stir it on its day. Do they not know that on Tuesday there is an hour; whoever coincides with it, his blood will not stop until he dies, or what Allah wills.'

key_terms.الْحِجَامَة: Cupping (a traditional medical practice involving suction)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Tuesday regarding cupping and blood according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the popular belief that Tuesday is the 'day of blood,' confirming that a specific hour on this day can cause bleeding to persist until death. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of reconciling folk wisdom with divine decree, illustrating how natural phenomena are governed by God's will rather than mere superstition. It serves as a practical guideline for medical practices like cupping, emphasizing caution during specific astrological or temporal windows.

en.hubeali: H 14671 – Al-Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Humraan who said:

Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘So in what do the people differ?’ I said, ‘They are alleging that the cupping (Al-Hajaamat) during the day of Tuesday is correct’. Heasws said to me: ‘And to what (direction) are they going with regards to that?’ I said, ‘They are alleging that it is the day of the blood’. Heasws said: ‘They are right. So it is more appropriate not to stir it in its day. But rather, know that during the day of Tuesday there is a particular time, if it coincides with it, his bleeding would not stop until he dies, or what Allahazwj so Desires’.
